sections.title: Snow ratio.
sections.note: Given the measured water, how far off is the snowfall? 1,197 hand-measured Sierra snow days, 2021 to 2026; each winter is scored by a model that never saw it.

sections.title: Rain or snow.
sections.note: Water wrongly called rain or snow per wet day, at 22 Tahoe snow sensors over 5,412 held-out days. The three methods are tied; calling everything snow would miss by 4.9 mm.

sections.title: Water.
sections.note: Model water against what 22 snow sensors measured, on the 2025 and 2026 winters held out in turn.
rows: Corrected to the snow sensors (in use)

sections.title: Water, Mammoth area.
sections.note: The same test against 10 snow sensors along the crest around Mammoth, on the 2024, 2025, and 2026 winters held out in turn. Mammoth Mountain and Sherwin Ridge use the Mammoth Pass sensor, Matterhorn Peak the Slide Canyon one, and Dana Plateau the Dana Meadows one; June Mountain, Carson Peak, and Mt. Whitney have no working sensor nearby and are left uncorrected.
rows: Corrected to the snow sensors (in use where a sensor is near)

sections.title: Water, Cascades.
sections.note: The same test against 10 snow sensors in the Washington Cascades and Olympics, on the 2024, 2025, and 2026 winters held out in turn. Crystal Mountain and White Pass use the curve pooled over all ten, which did better there than their own sensor's. Mt. Rainier, Mt. Baker, and Mt. St. Helens are shown their sensor but left uncorrected, since it sits far below the mountain; Glacier Peak and Mt. Adams have none.
rows: Corrected to the snow sensors (in use, except on the volcanoes)

sections.title: Rain or snow, Cascades.
sections.note: The same test at 64 snow sensors in the Washington Cascades and Olympics over 16,508 held-out days, 4,691 of them mixed. The Cascades' curve is centered at 0.75 C of wet-bulb against the Sierra's 1.25 C: more of each storm is rain. Calling everything snow would miss by 10.6 mm.

sections.title: Snow ratio, Cascades.
sections.note: The Sierra-trained ratio on 248 hand-measured snow days at 9 Washington stations, 2023 to 2026, none of which it was trained on. Refitting it with those days added did no better at a station held out (1.50 in), so the Sierra's is kept. It runs a little fluffy west of the crest and dense east of it.
rows: This site's ratio, trained in the Sierra (in use)

sections.title: Water, Tetons.
sections.note: The same test against 10 snow sensors from the Snake River's headwaters to the Gros Ventre, on the 2024, 2025, and 2026 winters held out in turn. Grand Targhee and Togwotee Pass use their own sensor and Jackson Hole and Teton Pass the Phillips Bench one; Snow King has none within reach and is left uncorrected.
rows: Corrected to the snow sensors (in use where a sensor is near)

sections.title: Rain or snow, Tetons.
sections.note: The same test at 18 snow sensors around the Tetons over 2,915 held-out days, 687 of them mixed. Nearly all of it is snow there: calling everything snow would miss by only 2.4 mm. The curve fitted there is centered at 0.75 C of wet-bulb and does no better than the Sierra's.

sections.title: Snow ratio, Tetons.
sections.note: 869 hand-measured snow days at 21 stations around Jackson, 2023 to 2026, where the snow averages 14 to 1. The Sierra-trained ratio already reads that from the cold, so adding the Teton days changes little; the one in use is scored here at stations it never saw.
rows: This site's ratio, trained in the Sierra
Trained on Sierra and Teton days together (in use)
